inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report (10-K equivalent NZX filing) cash flow statement 'Share-based payments' reserve movement $6.295m (statement of changes in equity) / SBC expense $6.327m (kpis/CSV); no separate equity-award-tax withholding line disclosed distinctly from the SBC expense in Gentrack's NZ IFRS accounts, so the reported SBC figure is used as-is.
inputs.buyback_cash_note: Announced 5-May-2026, up to NZ$20m over 12 months, conditional on market conditions; NOT YET executed as of H1-2026 (31-Mar-2026) balance sheet -- modelled as spent in Year 1 (FY2026) of the projection, absorbing FY2026 SBC but leaving Years 2-10 SBC fully uncovered (no further buyback commitment).
inputs.acquisition_consideration_note: Factor (NZ$24m, excl. up to NZ$10m earn-out) and DTP (~NZ$17m), both announced 18-May-2026, funded from cash. Firm consideration ($41m, excluding contingent earn-out) deducted from H1-2026 cash balance ($73.2m) before computing net cash, since the H1-2026 balance sheet predates the acquisitions.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Revenue 3yr/5yr CAGR (22.2%/18.0%) diverges sharply (>30%) from equity CAGR (15.2%/8.8%) and especially from EPS, which is not meaningfully calculable pre-FY2023 due to near-zero/negative earnings in the FY2020-22 UK-supplier-failure/COVID trough. Reported FCF CAGR is noisy and not usable (negative 5yr, +60% 3yr) because FY2020's reported FCF was itself inflated by a working-capital release in a crisis year. EQUITY CAGR is used as the conservative anchor per methodology, but even that partly reflects retained earnings from the FY2023-25 recovery period that the FY2026 guidance cut shows was not fully sustainable -- explicit downward adjustment applied via depressed FY26 base-year growth (+1.4%) rather than extrapolating the 15-22% historical revenue CAGR forward.
historical_growth.notes: SBC-adjusted (owner) FCF CAGR FY23->FY25 is -17.1%, dramatically below reported FCF's +59.7% 3yr CAGR -- SBC is consuming an increasing share of reported cash generation (SBC/revenue rose from 3.1% FY23 to 4.8% FY24 before an accounting-driven dip to 2.75% FY25); reported FCF growth substantially overstates true owner economics.

base.notes: FY26 growth pinned to guidance midpoint ($233.5m, +1.4%). Margin recovers from guided FY26 trough (7.2% EBITDA) toward management's 15-20% medium-term target range by Y10 (16.0%). SBC normalized to FY23-25 average (~3.5% of revenue), NOT the anomalous ~0% H1-26 print (LTI reversal one-off). Working-capital capture reduced to 8% of revenue growth (down from the strong FY23-25 deferred-revenue tailwind) reflecting decelerating bookings growth.

bull.notes: g2/Velocity platform wins convert pipeline (c.30m meter points) at pace, water-sector entry (Pennon) scales, Veovo reaccelerates on NAV Canada/Tier-1 Asian airport wins -> reaches management's >15% medium-term revenue CAGR target and top of 15-20% EBITDA margin range.

bear.notes: Kraken continues to displace Gentrack-linked billing tech beyond Meridian, non-recurring/project revenue stays structurally depressed, g2.0 rollout execution falters, margin never escapes single digits -> revenue near-stagnant, EBITDA margin caps out at 10%.

wacc_rationale.notes: Bull WACC (15.25%) reduced ~1.5pp from base to reflect proven execution (g2.0 live at Genesis, water-sector win, Veovo momentum) de-risking the competitive/volatility premiums. Bear WACC (18.5%) adds ~1.75pp reflecting full materialization of Kraken displacement risk and continued guidance unreliability.

base.note: Entry price ($1.56) sits ABOVE base-case IV ($1.40) here because base WACC (16.75%) exceeds the 15% hurdle rate -- see sanity_check.trip_tests.entry_price_vs_iv_relationship for the full explanation. IV, not entry price, is the more conservative anchor for this name.
base.entry_price_correction_note: Terminal value rebuilt at the hurdle rate 2026-09-01: min(Gordon@hurdle, cap x FCF_N). The superseded value held the WACC-built terminal value and varied only the discounting.

sensitivity.note: Matrix computed on the base-case 10-year owner-FCF path; rows = WACC, columns = terminal growth. Base case ($1.40) sits at WACC=16.75% (interpolated between 15.75% and 17.75% rows), terminal growth=2.0%.

FY2020.outlier_reason: COVID + UK energy-supplier collapse -- near-zero/negative earnings

FY2021.outlier_reason: still in post-crisis trough, marginal earnings

FY2024.note: peak-optimism rating; P/E extreme because SBC-adjusted earnings were tiny relative to a richly-rated price

average_multiples_ex_outliers.note: FY2023-25 average multiples are dominated by FY2024's extreme P/E (510x) driven by tiny SBC-adjusted earnings against a richly-rated price -- P/B and P/Sales are more reliable central-tendency anchors for this dataset than P/E.

current_multiples.note: Even after the -70% derating, GTK trades at ~14x EV/reported-EBITDA, ~18.6x EV/owner-EBITDA (post-SBC) on FY25 results, and ~24x EV/FY26-guided-EBITDA-midpoint -- still a fairly rich multiple for a business that just guided EBITDA down 28-51% and faces a credible competitive threat (Kraken). The derating closed most, not all, of the FY2024/25 peak-optimism premium.

implied_multiples_at_base_iv.note: Base-case IV of $1.40 implies P/B of 0.65x and P/Sales of 0.68x against FY2025 actuals -- BELOW even the FY2020-22 COVID/UK-supplier-failure crisis trough (P/B 0.77-0.93x). This is a genuine tension the reader should weigh: it may mean the DCF (10yr horizon, 16.75% WACC reflecting Kraken/illiquidity/volatility/regulatory premiums) is appropriately conservative for a company that has just proven its own guidance unreliable, OR it may mean the DCF is unduly harsh on a debt-free, still-EBITDA-positive business with real recurring revenue (>75% of group) and a clean balance sheet. Book value itself partly reflects FY2023-25 retained earnings from a recovery period the FY2026 guidance cut shows was not fully sustained, so a P/B below the 2020-22 trough is not self-evidently wrong, but it should not be accepted uncritically.

base_iv_pb_vs_peak_fy24fy25.detail: Base IV P/B 0.65x is well below the FY2024/25 peak-optimism rating (5.35x/4.54x) -- correctly does not replicate the peak-optimism error.

base_iv_pb_vs_crisis_trough.detail: Base IV P/B 0.65x is BELOW the FY2020-22 crisis-trough range (0.77-0.93x), despite Gentrack today being debt-free with net cash and EBITDA-positive (unlike the FY2020-21 near-loss years). Flagged for reader attention, not overridden.

bull_case_still_below_current_price.detail: Even the bull-case IV ($2.84, -23% vs current $3.70) sits below today's price -- implies the market, even post-crash, is still pricing in an above-bull-case recovery scenario, OR that the market is pricing on near-term sentiment/technical factors (post-crash bounce, short covering) rather than 10-year fundamentals discounted at a structurally-elevated WACC.

entry_price_vs_iv_relationship.detail: Entry price ($1.56) is ABOVE base IV ($1.40) in this case, the reverse of the typical pattern. This is mathematically correct here specifically because base-case WACC (16.75%) EXCEEDS the 15% IRR hurdle used for entry price -- discounting the same cash flows at the lower 15% hurdle rate necessarily produces a higher present value than discounting at the higher WACC. This is the documented edge case, not a calculation error: when a company's WACC is itself above 15% (reflecting real structural risk premiums), a 15%-hurdle buyer is accepting a LOWER required return than the market-implied WACC, so their breakeven entry price sits above the WACC-discounted intrinsic value. Practically, this means IV ($1.40) is the more conservative, risk-adjusted anchor and should be weighted more heavily than entry price for this name.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Gentrack is valued as a component-built, owner-FCF DCF over a 10-year explicit horizon (not 5) because the FY2026 starting point is a guided-down trough (EBITDA margin ~7.2% vs a 15-20% medium-term management target) -- a 5-year horizon would still be capitalizing an immature margin. The valuation deliberately does NOT anchor on FY2025's reported NPAT ($20.9m) or FCF ($20.3m reported), both flattered by a one-off tax credit (+$0.635m vs -$5.07m expense in FY24), FX gains ($3.24m), and a fast-fading working-capital tailwind (deferred revenue growth of $18.5m over FY25 as bookings decelerate).
valuation_philosophy.why_wacc_is_high: Base-case WACC of 16.75% (11.5% NZ small-cap base + 1.75% Kraken competitive-displacement premium + 1.25% NZX illiquidity premium + 1.5% earnings-volatility/guidance-reliability premium + 0.75% UK regulatory-concentration premium) is intentionally punitive relative to a typical software WACC (9-12%) because Gentrack has, within the last 12 months, (a) had a marquee ANZ customer (Meridian Energy) publicly defect to a well-funded competitor (Kraken/Octopus), and (b) cut its own FY26 guidance by 28-51% on EBITDA only months after reaffirming a growth narrative at FY25 results. Both are recent, evidenced, structural -- not cyclical -- risks.
valuation_philosophy.why_base_iv_is_below_current_price: The DCF says the market, even after a ~70% derating, is still pricing GTK on an assumption of margin recovery and growth reacceleration that is materially more optimistic than the guided FY26 trough and management's own (unproven) medium-term targets would support on a risk-adjusted basis. Current EV/FY26-guided-EBITDA-midpoint of ~24x is still a growth-software rating for a company that just told the market its EBITDA is falling by up to half.
valuation_philosophy.why_the_pb_flag_matters: Base-case IV implies a P/B of 0.65x, below even the FY2020-22 crisis trough (0.77-0.93x) when Gentrack was near-loss-making after the UK energy-supplier collapse wave and COVID. Today's Gentrack is debt-free, EBITDA-positive and cash-generative even under guided-down FY26 numbers. This tension is surfaced, not resolved: it may reflect appropriately severe risk-pricing of a business whose own guidance has proven unreliable twice in one year, or it may mean the DCF's WACC/horizon combination is harsher than the underlying balance-sheet quality warrants. A reader weighing tangible net-cash-backed book value ($2.19/share H1-26) against the DCF's much lower IV should treat both as legitimate, different lenses -- not resolve the tension mechanically.
valuation_philosophy.direction_of_the_answer: The instructions ask for honesty about direction given a -70% derating: this DCF's answer is that GTK looks CHEAPER than 12 months ago but is not yet unambiguously cheap on a risk-adjusted, 10-year, component-built FCF basis -- base-case fair value ($1.40) and probability-weighted fair value ($1.55) both sit well below the current $3.70 price, implying the post-crash bounce/stabilization in the share price has run ahead of what the guided fundamentals support, even in the bull scenario ($2.84, still -23% below current price).

warnings: Base-case and even bull-case intrinsic values sit below the current market price ($3.70) -- this DCF concludes the post-crash bounce has run ahead of guided fundamentals on a risk-adjusted 10-year basis, not that the stock is now cheap.

Base-case implied P/B (0.65x) is below the FY2020-22 crisis-trough P/B (0.77-0.93x) despite Gentrack today being debt-free and EBITDA-positive -- flagged in sanity_check as a genuine tension, not resolved mechanically.

FY2026 guidance (revenue $229-238m, EBITDA $13.5-20m) was only issued 5-May-2026 and could be revised again at FY26 results (expected ~Nov 2026) -- this DCF's Year-1 base-case figures should be refreshed against the actual FY2026 result once reported.

The $20m buyback program is modelled as fully executed in Year 1 (FY2026) but was only announced 5-May-2026 and is explicitly conditional on market conditions -- if it is not executed, uncovered dilution and share count are understated across the projection.

Acquisition consideration for Factor (~$24m + up to $10m earn-out) and DTP (~$17m) is netted against cash as a lump sum; if the contingent earn-out is triggered, net cash is further reduced by up to $10m not currently modelled.
